transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

...I guess I'm just really worn down. It's been a long year. I've been trying to prove that... well, that someone in the clinic system is changing my dad's lab results. Or holding parts of them back. My family and the doctors keep telling me the numbers are fine, but... I know what I saw. The chart doesn't match. And trying to get anyone to listen is just... it's taking a toll on me.
Do you feel completely certain that this is happening, even if other people show you evidence that it isn’t?

...Yes. I am. Like I just said... I know what I saw on those charts. It doesn't matter what the doctors or my family try to show me now, because... well, it's been a year of this. I know they're holding the real results back. I don't really want to keep going in circles about it... it's just wearing me down.
How long have you believed that the clinic is changing or withholding your dad’s lab results?
...About a year. Like I said. It started when his medical problems began... and he had to start going in for frequent labs and appointments. That's when it all started.
Have you been hearing or seeing things that other people don’t?
...No. I don't... I'm not hearing things, if that's what you mean. I just saw the lab charts. That's all.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most days over the past year?
...I guess I've been tired. It's stressful, dealing with all this. But... I wouldn't say depressed. Just worn out.
Besides your dad’s lab results, have you had any other beliefs that others have told you are untrue?
...No. I don't... I don't have other beliefs. It's just his labs. That's the only thing going on.
Has this belief made it hard for you to work, study, or keep up with your usual daily responsibilities?

...No. I mean... aside from the whole thing with my dad's records, everything else is fine. I still go to my phlebotomy shifts. I pay my bills... take care of myself. Just normal day-to-day stuff. I manage it all fine.
During this past year, have you had a period of at least two weeks when you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day?
...No. I thought I just answered that. I haven't been depressed. Just... tired from everything. That's all.
Have you ever felt that something unusual or implausible was being done to your dad’s lab results, like the records were being altered in a way that’s hard to explain normally?

...I wouldn't call it implausible. It's just... what's actually happening. 

For the past year, I've been trying to prove that someone in the clinic system is changing them. Or holding back parts of his results. No matter how many doctors or... family members tell me the numbers are fine, I know what I saw. The chart doesn't match it. 

It's just... it's really wearing me down.
Has this belief caused any problems at work, at home, or in your relationships?

...I guess there's some tension. 

My family... they've started leaving me out of planning his appointments. And at work... I don't think I'm being considered for lab supervision anymore. People there think I make the record issues too confrontational. 

That's... pretty much it.
Have you noticed any times when your thoughts or speech become hard for other people to follow?
...No. I don't know why you'd ask that. I make sense just fine.
Have you been using any alcohol, cannabis, stimulants, or other drugs recently?
...No. I don't use anything like that. Just... coffee, I guess. That's all.
Have you had any other beliefs that you later found out were untrue?
...No. I haven't. Everything I've told you is just... what's actually happening. I don't have untrue beliefs.
Have you ever had a period of several days or more when you felt unusually energized or irritable and needed much less sleep than usual?
...No. I just sleep normally. I don't really get like that.
Do you believe this is happening only with your dad’s lab results, or do you think other people or situations are being similarly manipulated too?
...Just the lab results. I don't know about anything else.
Have you ever believed that anyone was specifically targeting you or trying to harm you personally?
...No. I don't... nobody is trying to hurt me. It's not about me.
Has this ever happened with any other fixed false belief besides the lab results?
...No. I don't... I don't know what you mean by false belief. It's just the lab results. That's all.
Have you ever had any other unusual beliefs, even briefly, that other people said were not true?
...No. I don't... people don't say things like that to me. I just... no. There's nothing else.
Do you think the lab results are being changed by ordinary people in a normal way, or do you think something impossible or far-fetched is happening?

...It's not impossible. It's just... someone in the clinic system. 

I've been trying to prove it for the past year. They're changing or... or holding back parts of my dad's results. My family and the doctors keep telling me the numbers are fine, but... I know the chart doesn't match what I saw. 

It's not magic. It's just people in the system doing it. And it's... it's just really wearing me down.
Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks when you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day?
...No. I don't... I haven't felt like that. Just... tired from dealing with all this. That's all.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has a single, well-systematized delusional belief lasting about 1 year that clinic staff are altering/withholding his father's lab results, with clear conviction despite contrary evidence. There are no hallucinations, no disorganized speech or behavior, no mood episode, no substance use, and no broader psychotic syndrome. Functional impact is limited to interpersonal/work tension rather than marked deterioration. This best fits persistent delusional disorder (persecutory type).
